integrator_questions: Did line_loss_events fall below 2.0 on the s-bend and slalom at wheel_track 0.10 m? Where does the first loss occur on each track?
Did the oval finish rate hold near 0.75, or did the narrower track change it? Report completion_time for any finished run.
Did steering_oscillation rise with the narrower track, and does kd still damp it?
If line loss is 0 but max_error stays at or above 0.06, is the limit wheel-command saturation (+/-4095) or control response?

intent: Restore the iteration-4 geometry, the best design so far (291.9), and change only wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.10 m. I kept the 16 mm footprint out because it dropped the oval to 0 of 20 finishes and did not clear line loss. I expect line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom to fall below 2.0 and max_error to fall below 0.06, with the oval finish rate holding at or above 0.75. If line loss clears but max_error stays at or above 0.06, the next step is to consider a different lever, not a narrower track. If the oval finish rate drops or steering_oscillation rises sharply, I will return wheel_track to 0.12 m.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) the 16 mm footprint hurt the oval because the larger footprint blurs the centre signal, so 12 mm should be kept; (2) the remaining s-bend and slalom line loss is a turning-authority limit, which a narrower wheel_track should relieve; (3) a narrower track will raise steering_oscillation only modestly. Measurements requested per track: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort. line_loss_events separates coverage from control, and the oval finish rate checks that the change did not break the working configuration.
rationale: Iteration 6 tested the 16 mm footprint at the 50 mm span and y = 0.075 m. It scored 83.5, far below iteration 4's 291.9. The oval finished 0 of 20 runs, down from 15 of 20, and line_loss_events stayed at 2.0 on both the s-bend and the slalom, so the larger footprint did not clear the line loss. The Integrator's rule for this case says to return sensor_size to 0.012 m and keep the 50 mm span if the oval finish rate falls well below 0.75. That condition is met, so I am following that part of the advice. The Integrator also said that if line loss persists at 16 mm, the next lever is wheel_track 0.10 m. Turning authority is the one lever not yet tested in isolation, and the evidence (line loss of 2.0 on the bends at every footprint and span tried at the forward limit) is consistent with a turn-rate limit. I therefore restore the iteration-4 geometry and change only wheel_track, from 0.12 m to 0.10 m. A narrower track gives more turn rate per unit wheel difference (turn rate = difference / wheel_track). Because this is the single change from the best-scoring design, any change in the result can be attributed to the track width. I keep sensor_size 0.012 m, five sensors at x = -0.025 to +0.025 m, y = 0.075 m, the 0.03 m wheels, body_width 0.12 m, body_length 0.18 m and mass 0.6 kg. Body width and mass are unchanged because the off-track limit sits at its 0.06 m floor and neither is shown to limit the outcome. Expected result: line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom falls below 2.0, and max_error drops below 0.06 on the bends. The oval finish rate should stay near 0.75 or improve. Risk: a narrower track can reduce stability at speed and may raise steering_oscillation, so that is the watch point.
